histone H3 is not essential for chromatin assembly.

the nucleosome repeat length of chromatin is determined at the onset of assembly and that this length depends on the amount of histones H3 and H4 present in the system, and the amount of histine H1 added at the onset of chromatin assembly.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nucleosome repeat length in chromatin is a dynamic parameter that is a function of chromatin assembly conditions and of the availability of the different classes of histones, including histone H1.
the nucleosome repeat length is determined by the relative amounts of the histones present during chromatin assembly.
histone H3 and H1, but not histone H4, are the limiting factors in the chromatin assembly reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chromatin assembly can be used to generate chromatin with a defined nucleosome repeat length.
the chromatin assembly system of Xenopus oocyte extracts is an excellent model to study the assembly of chromatin with native internucleosome spacing.
